text:
anshul: quick question — should tenant-level pins accept a 'selector' (family/semver band) or only exact content-hash?

sam: family selector is friendlier. ops can still roll minor fixes. risk: ambiguity when family maps to multiple hashes.

vivian: agree we need explicit modes. suggest `pin_mode`: hard (content-hash), soft (family w/ auto patching), gated (family but control plane asks for approval on incompatible diffs).

joel: implementation constraints: routing determinism, capacity accounting, and observable resolution mapping. we must emit the resolved hash in telemetry.

carla: proposed schema: `pin_scope` (tenant|route|call), `selector_type` (exact|family|semver_band), `selector_value` (e.g. "luma-3.1"), `pin_mode` (hard|soft|gated), `fallback_strategy` (prefer_exact, prefer_family, weighted), `resolution_ttl`, `require_resolution_audit` (bool). example snippet:```json
{
  "pin_scope": "tenant",
  "selector_type": "family",
  "selector_value": "luma-3.1",
  "pin_mode": "soft",
  "fallback_strategy": "prefer_exact",
  "resolution_ttl": "300s",
  "require_resolution_audit": "true"
}
```

anshul: +1. migration: existing tenant pins default to `pin_mode=hard` and `selector_type=exact`.

vivian: also add `resolution_eligibility` label (e.g., allow/deny opt-in for patches flagged as breaking).

joel: infra ticket INF-7234 created for family index etag + family->hash change webhook. need O(1) resolution with watch-based cache.

infra-bot: INF-7234 created by joel.

anshul: action items: 1) carla to open schema PR with examples & migration notes. 2) joel to spec caching + telemetry events (family_resolution, fallback_applied). 3) vivian to write short migration playbook for customers. i'll link RFC and PR.

carla: will include curl and SDK examples for both gated and soft workflows.

sam: ship it when PR green and infra proves cheap resolution. :rocket:
